summary: Umatilla NF lookout in Umatilla County, Oregon; first pole tower 1914, present 92-ft steel tower dated 1929 or 1934 by sources, staffed each summer and still in service.

facts.design: 92-ft steel Aermotor tower (per FireLookout.com); CCC-built living quarters moved from Lucky Strike Lookout

events.note: First structure, a 60-ft pole tower with a 6x6 cab, per FireLookout.com
Register's date for the 92-ft tower built by the Forest Service; FireLookout.com dates its replacement to 1934
FireLookout.com says the present 92-ft Aermotor tower replaced the first structure

evidence.supports: name changed from Lookout Mountain to Tower Mountain in 1925
evidence.quote: Originally called Lookout Mountain, the name was changed to Tower Mountain in 1925 to avoid confusion with another Lookout Mountain nearby.

evidence.supports: location 18 miles ESE of Ukiah, Umatilla County, Umatilla NF
first structure was a 60-ft pole tower with 6x6 cab built in 1914
evidence.quote: The first structure was a 60' pole tower with 6x6' cab built in 1914.

evidence.supports: present 92-ft Aermotor steel tower replaced the first in 1934
evidence.quote: It was replaced by the present 92' Aermotor steel tower in 1934.

evidence.supports: Forest Service constructed the 92-ft tower in 1929
evidence.quote: The 92’ tower was constructed by the U.S. Forest Service in 1929, and the attractive CCC cabin living quarters was moved to the site from the old Lucky Strike Lookout in the late 1940s.

evidence.supports: elevation 6,812 ft (2,076 m); FireLookout.com gives 6850 ft

corrections.why: Both sources give a 92-foot tower (about 28 m); 1.8 m cannot be the tower height

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the Forest Service constructed the 92-ft tower in 1929; FireLookout.com says the present Aermotor tower replaced the 1914 structure in 1934. The story reports both and does not settle the question.
NHLR gives 6,812 ft (2,076 m); FireLookout.com gives 6850 ft. The record keeps NHLR's 2076.3 m.

notes_for_editor: Present tower date conflicts (1929 NHLR vs 1934 FireLookout.com); no Forest Service primary record checked. Aermotor make comes only from FireLookout.com. Access and visiting rules not found. Recorded height of 1.8 m corrected to 92 ft. NHLR visit reports are volunteer-written and used only lightly. Fact-check 2026-10-08: story reworded where it went beyond the sources ("today" staffing); Umatilla National Forest and US 142, OR 20 evidence added.
